# Ostler

> Ostler is an open-source MCP browser for AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. It checks its own work: research answers cite only pages it actually read, with every quote verified, forms are filled in one call with every value read back, and Qdrant remembers what worked.

Ostler is one local Rust binary (Apache-2.0) that runs Chrome and speaks MCP over stdio to coding agents and A2A over HTTP to other agents. It has no LLM inside, no cloud browser and no anti-bot evasion. Status: v0.2, early; tested against real Chrome and Qdrant on local fixtures, not yet benchmarked on the open web.

Key facts:

- Install: `cargo install --git https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler ostler`, then `ostler setup claude --apply` (Claude Code), or see the agents page for Codex, Cursor and VS Code.
- Requirements: Rust 1.89+ and Chrome or Chromium. Prebuilt binaries arrive with the first tagged release.
- Evidence: local fixtures; a five-task scripted comparison with Playwright MCP and Chrome DevTools MCP; seven live public practice pages. Not yet measured on the open web.
- Research: `read` returns the best passages for a query; `cite` marks a quote VERIFIED only if its words are on a page read this session; `evidence` lists citations and the pages that could not be read (paywall, bot wall, robots.txt).
- Forms: `form_fill` fills a whole form in one call and reads every value back; 3 tool calls instead of 22 on a 20-field form (same engine, one call per field; scripted, model-free, local fixtures).
- Memory: optional, in Qdrant or an encrypted local file; stores facts you save and per-site playbooks (structure, not values). Secret-looking values are refused; detection is heuristic.
- Safety: page text is fenced as untrusted, a domain allowlist holds every request, CAPTCHAs are handed to a person.

## Docs

- [Quickstart](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/quickstart.html): Install, check, connect, and fill a demo form in five minutes.
- [Install](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/install.html): Every way to get the binary, what works today, update and uninstall.
- [Use with your agent](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/agents.html): Add Ostler as an MCP browser to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code or any MCP client, with a forms and a research workflow.
- [Cookbook](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/cookbook.html): Recipes: deep research with checked citations, reading, QA, logins, forms, approvals and A2A, with what is not built yet.
- [Forms and verification](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/forms.html): How keys become fields, how values are verified by read-back, and what submit results mean.
- [Memory and privacy](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/memory.html): What is stored, what sealing hides and does not, local embeddings, per-tenant tokens.
- [Configuration and CLI](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/configuration.html): Config file, environment variables, every serve and a2a flag.
- [Tools reference](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/tools.html): All 30 MCP tools: browse, read and cite, search, extract, forms and memory, with parameters and profiles.
- [Security model](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/security.html): The threat model: what Ostler does, and what it does not do.
- [A2A](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/a2a.html): Let other agents hand Ostler forms over Agent2Agent v1.0.
- [Architecture](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/architecture.html): Crates, the injected runtime, the form model, and the decisions behind them.
- [Benchmarks](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/benchmarks.html): Measured on local fixtures with a scripted agent. Read the caveats.
- [Economics](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/economics.html): Unit costs, scaling limits, the moat question and what could go wrong.
- [Design review](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/review.html): The October 2026 review: five design flaws and their status.
- [Troubleshooting](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/troubleshooting.html): Symptoms, causes and fixes. Start with ostler doctor.
- [Changelog](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/changelog.html): What changed, including the Unreleased section.
